speaker: Doctor
text: Since the spinning sensation is constant, I need to check for associated symptoms. Have you experienced any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or recent episodes of vomiting?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty with balance or coordination when you try to walk or stand still? Also, have you noticed any weakness or numbness on one side of your body, or any changes in your speech?

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or tenderness behind your ears, or have you had a recent viral illness like a cold or flu? Also, does the spinning sensation worsen when you move your head or change positions?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the constant vertigo following a viral illness and lack of hearing symptoms, I suspect vestibular neuritis. Let me check your eye movements for nystagmus to confirm.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Please look straight ahead at my nose, then slowly move your eyes to the left and right without moving your head. I am checking for involuntary eye movements known as nystagmus, which would support a diagnosis of vestibular neuritis.

speaker: Patient
text: I'm doing my best to follow your nose with just my eyes. It feels a bit strange, but I don't feel any sudden jerking or spinning in my vision.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have constant vertigo without hearing loss or positional triggers, vestibular neuritis remains the most likely diagnosis. I will now proceed to finalize my assessment based on these clinical findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Vestibular Neuritis
